residencyRequirements.description: The petitioner must have been a resident and actual inhabitant of the State of Oklahoma for at least six (6) months immediately preceding the filing and a resident of the county of filing for at least thirty (30) days. (43 O.S. §102)

waitingPeriod.description: Oklahoma has a mandatory 90-day waiting period if the parties have minor children born of the marriage, or a 10-day waiting period if there are no minor children. (43 O.S. §107.1)

fault.name: Wife Pregnant at Marriage by Another
fault.description: When the wife at the time of marriage was pregnant by another person

fault.name: Imprisonment
fault.description: Imprisonment of the other party in a state or federal penal institution under a sentence thereto at the time the petition is filed

fault.name: Insanity
fault.description: Insanity for a period of five (5) years, the insane person having been an inmate of a state institution for the insane for such period

fault.name: Living Apart
fault.description: The husband and wife have lived separate and apart without cohabitation for a continuous period of two (2) years by reason of incompatibility

groundsForDissolution.notes: Oklahoma recognizes both fault and no-fault grounds. Incompatibility is the most commonly used ground. The full list of grounds is set forth in 43 O.S. §101.

propertyDivision.description: Oklahoma courts divide jointly-acquired property in a just and reasonable manner. Property acquired by either spouse during the marriage through joint industry is subject to equitable division. Property owned before the marriage, or acquired by gift or inheritance, is generally separate property.
propertyDivision.separateProperty: Property owned before the marriage or acquired by gift or inheritance is separate property and is not subject to division, although commingling or use during the marriage may change its character.

filingFees.notes: Oklahoma filing fees for divorce range from approximately $183 to $273 depending on the county. Fee waivers are available for qualifying low-income individuals via an Affidavit of Indigency.

basic.name: Entry of Appearance / Waiver
basic.description: Respondent waives formal service and enters an appearance

basic.name: Decree of Divorce
basic.description: Final court order dissolving the marriage

service.name: Summons
service.description: Formal service on respondent via sheriff, process server, or certified mail
alternatives: Waiver of Service / Entry of Appearance

service.name: Waiver of Service / Entry of Appearance
service.description: Respondent waives formal service and enters an appearance
service.notes: Must be signed by respondent and filed with the court

withChildren.name: Parenting Plan
withChildren.description: Proposed custody, visitation, and decision-making arrangement

withChildren.name: Child Support Computation
withChildren.description: Calculation per Oklahoma Child Support Guidelines (43 O.S. §118D, §119)

withChildren.name: Affidavit of Income and Expenses
withChildren.description: Sworn statement of each party's income and expenses for support calculation

inState.description: Respondent must file an answer within 20 days of service within Oklahoma

outOfState.description: Respondent served outside Oklahoma must file an answer within 30 days of service

childSupportGuidelines.description: Oklahoma uses an income shares model. Both parents' gross monthly incomes are combined and the child support obligation is determined from the Oklahoma Child Support Guidelines schedule based on combined adjusted gross income and the number of children.
childSupportGuidelines.notes: The court may deviate from the guidelines upon a finding that application would be unjust or inappropriate. Credits may apply for overnight visitation.

maintenanceGuidelines.description: Oklahoma courts may award alimony (support and maintenance) to either party. The court considers factors including the duration of the marriage, the earning capacity of each party, the standard of living during the marriage, the age and health of the parties, and the ability of the supporting spouse to pay. Alimony may be awarded as a lump sum, periodic payments, or both.
maintenanceGuidelines.eligibility: Either party may request alimony. The court has broad discretion in determining the amount and duration based on the circumstances of the case.

court.name: District Court
court.description: Divorce is filed in the District Court in the county where the petitioner has resided for at least 30 days.
